page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a memory-allocated virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 machine family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 26.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the hardware exhibits modest performance characteristics. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, falls into the lower tier, with scores of 1109.89 and 2914.17 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 162.39 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 25.86 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 21.97 GB/sec for large-block writes. Computational benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core (924.0) and multi-core (2032.0), as well as Passmark CPU (3477.62), consistently place this instance in the lower performance brackets.

From a workload perspective, the n1-highmem-4 is designed for memory-intensive applications that do not require high-frequency compute or advanced vector extensions like AVX-512, which are absent. It is suitable for moderate database operations, caching layers such as Redis, where it achieves 2.75 million SET operations per second, and basic web serving. The qualitative cost profile reflects an older hardware generation, offering a cost-effective option for legacy workloads or development environments requiring more memory than standard general-purpose instances without the premium of newer architecture classes.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine from the N1 family, configured with 4 vCPUs and 26.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz with 2 physical cores and hyper-threading, this instance provides 6.5 GB of memory per core. It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs. Performance benchmarks indicate modest capabilities, with a Passmark CPU score of 3477.62 and a Redis SET throughput of 2.75 million operations per second. Lacking advanced instruction sets like AVX-512, it is appropriate for memory-demanding but compute-light workloads, such as caching layers, small databases, and general-purpose applications requiring a higher memory-to-vCPU ratio.
